summary.one_liner: A Python CLI (gpte) that generates and iteratively improves code projects from a natural-language prompt file using LLMs such as OpenAI and Anthropic models.
summary.what_it_does: You write a prompt file describing software in plain language and run the gpte command on a project folder; the tool has an AI write and execute the code. Running gpte with -i against an existing folder asks the AI to implement improvements to code already there. Pre-prompts (the agent's instructions) can be overridden with a custom preprompts folder via --use-custom-preprompts, which the README says is how the agent remembers things between projects. Image inputs such as architecture or UX diagrams can be passed with --image_directory when a vision-capable model is used. The package also installs a bench binary for benchmarking custom agents against APPS and MBPP. The README says it supports OpenAI, Azure OpenAI and Anthropic models, and that open source models like WizardCoder can be run with extra setup.
use_cases: generate a new project from a text prompt
improve or extend existing code with an AI
benchmark a custom coding agent on APPS or MBPP
add diagrams as context for code generation
experiment with AI code generation pipelines
how_to_run: Create an empty project folder containing a file named 'prompt' with your instructions
notable: Generates code from a natural-language prompt file and can then improve existing code with -i
Customizable agent behavior through overridable preprompts folder
Accepts image inputs for vision-capable models
Installs a bench command for benchmarking custom agents on APPS and MBPP
Maintainers point to aider as the well-maintained hackable CLI and to gptengineer.app as the managed service
caveats: Requires an API key from a supported model provider unless a custom local model is configured, which the README only describes as documented elsewhere
README describes the project as an experimentation platform; the maintainers point users to aider for a well-maintained CLI
Python 3.8-3.9 are no longer supported; the last version supporting them was 0.2.6
